claims.statement: langgraph.json registers the `chess` graph as the factory `apps/server/langchain_chess_server/graph.py:make_graph` and the custom HTTP app as `apps/server/langchain_chess_server/app.py:app`.

For a run (runtime.execution_runtime present), make_graph calls resolve_context(config, runtime) and then build_graph with a ranker factory from pooled_ranker(ServerSettings()), building fresh ServerSettings per run; assistant context reaches the graph only through the runtime argument.

build_agent now lives in libs/systemone (langchain_chess_systemone.agent) and is shared by surfaces; the server's build_graph calls it with server_model as model factory, the given ranker factory, GameSetupMiddleware as surface middleware (after System 1), fixed_topology=True, context_schema=ChessContextInput and the default name `chess`. build_agent passes no model for `systemone`, adds one SystemOneMiddleware for `systemone` and `hybrid`, and NoSystemOne for `llm` under a fixed topology.
Building the chess graph never calls a model or the System 1 classifier.

When policy is `systemone`, the shared systemone() builder creates SystemOneMiddleware with threshold and tournament_threshold forced to 0.0 and has_model=False regardless of settings, so System 1 always plays; for hybrid the settings' thresholds apply.
Each TypeSafeClassifier is built per graph build but takes its sync and async HTTP clients from a process-wide ClientPool (POOL, 15 second timeout), so all classifiers share one connection pair.

The server's server_model calls langchain_chess.chat_models.chat_model with arguments resolved for the `server` surface; chat_model calls init_chat_model with max_tokens set to model_kwargs' limit or an output budget (MAX_TOKENS 64000, capped by the model's output limit and half of a smaller window), a name set to the bare model name so gateway traces don't all read as ChatOpenAI, a reasoning effort only when set, and a profile whose max_input_tokens is the known context window minus the budget (gateway models the price snapshot doesn't know get no profile).

memory is a boolean effective only with a model; with a model and memory=True, build_agent raises a ChessContractError (the model can't use memory; turn it off) when the model has no known input limit in its profile, while systemone with memory=True still builds.

ChessContext (version 2) defaults are policy `hybrid`, model `langsmith:baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, model_kwargs {}, reasoning_effort None, system_prompt None, show_fen and show_board True, move_list `both`, memory False, draw_claims `auto`, systemone_model `semif-qwen3.5-4b`, style `rich`, with_eval and with_nouls False, gate `margin`, threshold 0.9, tournament_threshold None, k 5, top_p None, seed 0.

Each ChessContext field is declared through setting(), which attaches json_schema_extra `langgraph_nodes` naming the nodes it affects (so Studio highlights them) plus the web app's x-label and x-help.

resolve_context reads assistant context (dict or pydantic model) and config configurable, treats a source without a version as the current VERSION, migrates each with migrate(unknown='drop') so unknown keys such as thread_id are dropped, and merges them with resolve so configurable wins, omitted keys keep the assistant value, an explicit None resets a key to its default, and the result is strictly validated so bad values fail the run up front.

The web client's configurableOf sends version plus every setting key as configurable on every submit, and its ChessContext types, defaults and specs are generated from the Python schema by langchain_chess_server.codegen into packages/chess-ui/src/generated, with a test failing when the committed files are stale.
ServerSettings reads the shell then `.env`, rejects any of LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_BASE_URL that is set but blank, and holds no model credentials itself.
TypeSafe settings are required only when the System 1 ranker factory runs: an llm-only graph builds without TYPESAFE_API_KEY while hybrid raises ValueError.
GET /ui/config returns the graph id `chess`, ChessContext.model_json_schema(), and dump(ChessContext()) as defaults.
The UI is mounted under /ui rather than / because custom routes shadow the Agent Server's own routes and / is its health check; /ui redirects to /ui/.
The static UI is mounted with app.mount and StaticFiles instead of app.frontend(), because frontend routes are low priority and the Agent Server's own /ui mount would answer first.
The static mount happens only when the Vite build directory exists (produced in CI before deploy); otherwise /ui/ returns a 404 JSON hint while /ui/config still answers.

model_limit builds default_model(ChessContext(model=model)) through the shared chat_model factory and returns its input limit, or None when the model has no known limit or cannot be built; it is exposed as GET /ui/model-limit, which requires a `model` query parameter, and the web client's fetchModelLimit maps the answer to known, none (null limit) or failed (request or body error) for the new-game dialog's decision whether to offer memory.

When the Agent Server calls make_graph without an execution runtime (state reads, updates, graph introspection), it returns shape(): a chess graph with no model, NoSystemOne and a never-written GameSetupMiddleware, which needs no clients or credentials.

Every build of the chess graph has the same nodes regardless of settings: with fixed_topology the llm policy uses NoSystemOne (named SystemOneMiddleware, same state schema, no-op hook), create_chess_agent keeps a no-op summarization node when memory is off, and GameSetupMiddleware is always present; tests assert run and read graphs have identical topology for every policy and memory.

ClientPool creates its client pair lazily under a lock so concurrent first uses make one pair, and aclose closes the pair so the next get makes a fresh one; the FastAPI app's lifespan (merged by the Agent Server with its own) calls POOL.aclose on shutdown.

The client pool lives in its own module imported by package name because langgraph loads graph.py by file path under a generated module name; a pool kept in graph.py would exist once per copy, and a test checks that shutdown closes the clients of a path-loaded graph.py.
ChessContext numeric knobs are bounded and validated at resolution: threshold and tournament_threshold in [0, 1], k from 1 to CHOICE_LIMIT (255), top_p in (0, 1], seed within ±(2^53−1).

GameSetupMiddleware writes a `setup` state key holding dump() of the run's resolved ChessContext (every current-version key including version and model_kwargs as given) only on the game's first turn (no existing setup, exactly one turn, opened by this run), in both before_agent and after_agent; later runs never overwrite it, a failed first turn still records it, a rejected first input records none, and threads from before setup existed never gain one.

The web client continues a game from its thread by reading `setup` through recordedContext, which uses loadRecorded to accept it only when it has exactly its version's keys, all valid, migrating it to the current version rather than filling in defaults.

The graph's context_schema is ChessContextInput, a lenient TypedDict with every key optional and nullable, so LangGraph builds context without validating and assistants saved by older versions still run; resolve performs validation.
build_graph attaches run metadata from sent(settings, 'server'): the reasoning_effort actually sent and max_tokens when model_kwargs set one, or only reasoning_effort None for the systemone policy.

On the server surface model_kwargs may set only allowlisted top-level arguments (temperature, top_p, max-tokens aliases, reasoning_effort, reasoning, verbosity, extra_body) and never account resources such as tools or prompt, even inside extra_body; violations raise when server_model builds the model.
The shared build_agent calls only the factories a policy uses, so model_kwargs go unread (and unchecked against the server surface) when the policy is systemone.
A run that fails while building the graph (e.g. a hybrid run without TypeSafe keys) ends in error before writing any state, and its thread still reads as empty values with no next nodes.

Under a real offline langgraph dev, a run paused before summarization reads back with the same next nodes and the graph the server describes has the nodes of the graph that ran, whether settings came from run config or assistant context.

render.html is a second Vite build input written into the server's static directory with base /ui/, so the /ui StaticFiles mount serves LangSmith's positions-dataset output renderer at /ui/render.html without a dedicated route.
